AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: >-
  FSx for ONTAP Content-Level PII Classification Scanner (CSF 2.0 Identify).
  Scans files via an S3 Access Point using Amazon Comprehend
  DetectPiiEntities. QUICK START: leave VpcId empty to deploy outside any
  VPC — this is the simplest path and requires only an internet-origin S3
  Access Point (check with `aws s3control get-access-point --account-id
  <id> --name <ap-name> --query NetworkOrigin`; "Internet" works with the
  default parameters below, "VPC" requires setting VpcId/SubnetIds/
  SecurityGroupId/RouteTableIds to the VPC the access point is bound to).
  No FSx control-plane API calls are made by this stack, so it has no
  dependency on any FSx Interface VPC Endpoint even when VpcId is set.
  Stack name pattern: fsxn-content-classification

Parameters:
  VpcId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      VPC ID to run the scanner Lambda inside. Leave empty (default) to
      deploy outside any VPC — the simplest path, and the only requirement
      is that the access_point_arn you invoke with is an Internet-origin
      S3 Access Point (verify with `aws s3control get-access-point
      --account-id <account-id> --name <ap-name> --query NetworkOrigin`).
      Set this ONLY if the access_point_arn you plan to scan is VPC-scoped
      (NetworkOrigin=VPC, e.g., one created by restore-verification.yaml's
      AttachAccessPoint step) — a VPC-scoped access point has no route from
      outside its bound VPC, so the Lambda must run inside that same VPC.
      When set, also set SubnetIds/SecurityGroupId/RouteTableIds below to
      match that VPC.
    Default: ''
    AllowedPattern: '^(vpc-[0-9a-f]{8,17})?$'

  SubnetIds:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Description: >-
      Private subnet IDs for the scanner Lambda. Required if VpcId is set;
      ignored otherwise. Leave as the default single empty-string entry
      when VpcId is empty.
    Default: ''

  SecurityGroupId:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      Security Group ID for the scanner Lambda (egress to VPC Endpoints).
      Required if VpcId is set; ignored otherwise.
    Default: ''
    AllowedPattern: '^(sg-[0-9a-f]{8,17})?$'

  RouteTableIds:
    Type: CommaDelimitedList
    Description: >-
      Route table IDs associated with SubnetIds. Used to attach the S3 and
      DynamoDB Gateway VPC Endpoints the scanner needs when running inside
      a VPC. Required if VpcId is set and CreateVpcEndpoints=true; ignored
      otherwise.
    Default: ''

  CreateVpcEndpoints:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      When VpcId is set, create VPC Endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB (Gateway)
      plus Comprehend and SNS (Interface) so the in-VPC scanner Lambda can
      reach the access point, report table, PII detection API, and
      notifications. Set to 'false' if your VPC already has all four —
      check first with `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters
      Name=vpc-id,Values=<your-vpc-id>` (a second Interface Endpoint for a
      service that already has one fails with a PrivateDnsEnabled conflict
      and rolls back this whole stack). If reusing restore-verification.
      yaml's VPC: that stack creates Secrets Manager/STS/FSx/S3-Gateway
      endpoints, none of which overlap with this stack's Comprehend/
      DynamoDB/SNS/S3-Gateway set except S3 — if that stack's
      CreateS3GatewayEndpoint was 'true', check for that existing S3
      Gateway Endpoint before setting this to 'true' (a second S3 Gateway
      Endpoint bound to the same route tables is rejected as a duplicate).
      Ignored if VpcId is empty.
    Default: 'true'
    AllowedValues: ['true', 'false']

  LambdaMemorySize:
    Type: Number
    Description: Lambda memory size in MB for the scanner function
    Default: 512
    AllowedValues: [256, 512, 1024, 2048]

  LambdaTimeoutSeconds:
    Type: Number
    Description: >-
      Lambda timeout in seconds. Scanning many/large files against
      Comprehend can take time — size this to your expected file count.
    Default: 600
    MinValue: 60
    MaxValue: 900

  DefaultLanguageCode:
    Type: String
    Description: Default Amazon Comprehend language code for DetectPiiEntities
    Default: en
    AllowedValues: [en, es, fr, de, it, pt, ar, hi, ja, ko, zh, zh-TW]

  DefaultMaxFiles:
    Type: Number
    Description: Default cap on files scanned per invocation (cost/runtime control)
    Default: 500
    MinValue: 1
    MaxValue: 10000

  NotificationTopicArn:
    Type: String
    Description: >-
      SNS Topic ARN for classification report notifications. Leave empty
      to skip notifications.
    Default: ''

Conditions:
  HasNotificationTopic: !Not [!Equals [!Ref NotificationTopicArn, '']]
  HasVpc: !Not [!Equals [!Ref VpcId, '']]
  ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints: !And
    - !Condition HasVpc
    - !Equals [!Ref CreateVpcEndpoints, 'true']

Resources:
  # ================================================================
  # VPC Endpoints — only created when VpcId is set and
  # CreateVpcEndpoints=true. Required so the in-VPC scanner Lambda can
  # reach: the VPC-scoped S3 Access Point being scanned (S3 Gateway), the
  # DynamoDB report table (DynamoDB Gateway), Comprehend DetectPiiEntities
  # (Comprehend Interface), and SNS notifications (SNS Interface).
  # ================================================================
  S3GatewayVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.s3'
      VpcEndpointType: Gateway
      RouteTableIds: !Ref RouteTableIds

  DynamoDbGatewayVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.dynamodb'
      VpcEndpointType: Gateway
      RouteTableIds: !Ref RouteTableIds

  ComprehendVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.comprehend'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      SubnetIds: !Ref SubnetIds
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true

  SnsVpcEndpoint:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      ServiceName: !Sub 'com.amazonaws.${AWS::Region}.sns'
      VpcEndpointType: Interface
      SubnetIds: !Ref SubnetIds
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !Ref VpcEndpointSecurityGroup
      PrivateDnsEnabled: true

  VpcEndpointSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Condition: ShouldCreateVpcEndpoints
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Allow scanner Lambda to access Interface VPC Endpoints (Comprehend, SNS)
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 443
          ToPort: 443
          SourceSecurityGroupId: !Ref SecurityGroupId
          Description: Lambda SG to VPC Endpoint (HTTPS)

  # ================================================================
  # DynamoDB — classification report ledger
  # ================================================================
  ClassificationReportTable:
    Type: AWS::DynamoDB::Table
    Properties:
      TableName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-reports'
      BillingMode: PAY_PER_REQUEST
      AttributeDefinitions:
        - AttributeName: access_point_arn
          AttributeType: S
        - AttributeName: started_at
          AttributeType: S
      KeySchema:
        - AttributeName: access_point_arn
          KeyType: HASH
        - AttributeName: started_at
          KeyType: RANGE
      PointInTimeRecoverySpecification:
        PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled: true
      SSESpecification:
        SSEEnabled: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Project
          Value: fsxn-observability
        - Key: Purpose
          Value: content-classification-report

  # ================================================================
  # Lambda Execution Role
  # ================================================================
  ScannerLambdaRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-lambda-role'
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      # Attached unconditionally — harmless when VpcId is empty (the
      # scanner Lambda simply won't have ENIs to manage), and avoids a
      # Fn::If on ManagedPolicyArns.
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: ContentClassificationPolicy
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Sid: S3AccessPointObjectRead
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - s3:ListBucket
                  - s3:GetObject
                Resource:
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:accesspoint/*'
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:s3:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:accesspoint/*/object/*'
              - Sid: ComprehendDetectPii
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - comprehend:DetectPiiEntities
                Resource: '*'
                # DetectPiiEntities does not support resource-level
                # permissions (it is a synchronous, stateless inference
                # API with no addressable resource).
              - Sid: DynamoDbReportLedger
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - dynamodb:PutItem
                Resource: !GetAtt ClassificationReportTable.Arn
              - Sid: SNSPublish
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - sns:Publish
                Resource: !If
                  - HasNotificationTopic
                  - !Ref NotificationTopicArn
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:sns:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*'
              - Sid: CloudWatchLogs
                Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: !Sub 'arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-scanner:*'

  ScannerLogGroup:
    Type: AWS::Logs::LogGroup
    Properties:
      LogGroupName: !Sub '/aws/lambda/${AWS::StackName}-scanner'
      RetentionInDays: 365  # classification reports double as CSF 2.0 Identify evidence

  # ================================================================
  # Lambda — Content Classification Scanner
  # ================================================================
  ScannerFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      FunctionName: !Sub '${AWS::StackName}-scanner'
      Runtime: python3.12
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      MemorySize: !Ref LambdaMemorySize
      Timeout: !Ref LambdaTimeoutSeconds
      Role: !GetAtt ScannerLambdaRole.Arn
      # Only set VpcConfig when VpcId is provided. A VPC-scoped S3 Access
      # Point (e.g., from restore-verification.yaml's AttachAccessPoint
      # step) has no route from outside its bound VPC, so scanning one
      # requires this Lambda to run inside that VPC — see the Description
      # above and Security Considerations in content-classification-scanner.md.
      VpcConfig: !If
        - HasVpc
        - SubnetIds: !Ref SubnetIds
          SecurityGroupIds:
            - !Ref SecurityGroupId
        - !Ref 'AWS::NoValue'
      Environment:
        Variables:
          REPORT_TABLE_NAME: !Ref ClassificationReportTable
          DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_CODE: !Ref DefaultLanguageCode
          DEFAULT_MAX_FILES: !Ref DefaultMaxFiles
          NOTIFICATION_TOPIC_ARN: !If [HasNotificationTopic, !Ref NotificationTopicArn, '']
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          """Content-level PII discovery scanner (CSF 2.0 Identify function).

          Invocation input (direct Lambda invoke or Step Functions task):
          {
              "access_point_arn": "arn:aws:s3:...:accesspoint/...",  // required
              "language_code": "en",                                  // optional
              "max_files": 500                                        // optional
          }

          Scans scannable text/structured-data files exposed via the given
          S3 Access Point for PII entities using Amazon Comprehend
          DetectPiiEntities, aggregates findings, writes a report to
          DynamoDB, and optionally notifies via SNS.

          Does NOT create or manage the S3 Access Point itself — pass the
          ARN of an existing one (e.g., from restore-verification.yaml's
          AttachAccessPoint step, or any other FSx for ONTAP S3 Access Point
          you want to classify).
          """
          import json
          import logging
          import os
          from dataclasses import dataclass, field
          from datetime import datetime, timezone
          from typing import Any

          import boto3
          from botocore.exceptions import ClientError

          logger = logging.getLogger()
          logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

          s3 = boto3.client("s3")
          comprehend = boto3.client("comprehend")
          dynamodb = boto3.resource("dynamodb")
          sns = boto3.client("sns")

          COMPREHEND_MAX_BYTES = 100_000
          CHUNK_SAFETY_MARGIN_BYTES = 2_000
          CHUNK_TARGET_BYTES = COMPREHEND_MAX_BYTES - CHUNK_SAFETY_MARGIN_BYTES

          SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS = frozenset({
              ".txt", ".csv", ".tsv", ".json", ".xml", ".log", ".md",
              ".yaml", ".yml", ".ini", ".conf", ".sql", ".html", ".htm",
          })

          DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_BYTES = 5_000_000
          DEFAULT_SAMPLE_BYTES = 500_000

          COMPREHEND_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES = frozenset({
              "en", "es", "fr", "de", "it", "pt", "ar", "hi", "ja", "ko", "zh", "zh-TW",
          })

          def _chunk_text(text, target_bytes=CHUNK_TARGET_BYTES):
              if not text:
                  return []
              chunks = []
              current_lines, current_bytes = [], 0
              for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
                  line_bytes = len(line.encode("utf-8"))
                  if line_bytes > target_bytes:
                      if current_lines:
                          chunks.append("".join(current_lines))
                          current_lines, current_bytes = [], 0
                      encoded = line.encode("utf-8")
                      for i in range(0, len(encoded), target_bytes):
                          chunks.append(encoded[i:i + target_bytes].decode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
                      continue
                  if current_bytes + line_bytes > target_bytes and current_lines:
                      chunks.append("".join(current_lines))
                      current_lines, current_bytes = [], 0
                  current_lines.append(line)
                  current_bytes += line_bytes
              if current_lines:
                  chunks.append("".join(current_lines))
              return chunks

          def _classify_object(access_point_arn, key, size_bytes, language_code):
              sampled = size_bytes > DEFAULT_MAX_FILE_BYTES
              finding = {"key": key, "size_bytes": size_bytes, "sampled": sampled,
                         "entity_counts": {}, "highest_confidence_by_type": {}, "error": ""}

              try:
                  if sampled:
                      resp = s3.get_object(Bucket=access_point_arn, Key=key,
                                           Range=f"bytes=0-{DEFAULT_SAMPLE_BYTES - 1}")
                  else:
                      resp = s3.get_object(Bucket=access_point_arn, Key=key)
                  raw = resp["Body"].read()
              except ClientError as e:
                  finding["error"] = f"read_failed: {e}"
                  return finding

              text = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
              if not text.strip():
                  return finding

              for chunk in _chunk_text(text):
                  if not chunk.strip():
                      continue
                  try:
                      resp = comprehend.detect_pii_entities(Text=chunk, LanguageCode=language_code)
                  except ClientError as e:
                      finding["error"] = f"comprehend_failed: {e}"
                      continue
                  for entity in resp.get("Entities", []):
                      etype = entity.get("Type", "UNKNOWN")
                      score = entity.get("Score", 0.0)
                      finding["entity_counts"][etype] = finding["entity_counts"].get(etype, 0) + 1
                      finding["highest_confidence_by_type"][etype] = max(
                          finding["highest_confidence_by_type"].get(etype, 0.0), score
                      )

              return finding

          def lambda_handler(event: dict[str, Any], context: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
              access_point_arn = event["access_point_arn"]
              language_code = event.get("language_code", os.environ.get("DEFAULT_LANGUAGE_CODE", "en"))
              max_files = int(event.get("max_files", os.environ.get("DEFAULT_MAX_FILES", "500")))

              if language_code not in COMPREHEND_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES:
                  raise ValueError(
                      f"Unsupported language_code '{language_code}' — must be one of "
                      f"{sorted(COMPREHEND_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES)}"
                  )

              started_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
              files_scanned = 0
              files_skipped_unscannable = 0
              files_sampled_too_large = 0
              files_with_pii = 0
              pii_density_by_type = {}
              findings = []

              paginator = s3.get_paginator("list_objects_v2")
              for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=access_point_arn, MaxKeys=1000):
                  for obj in page.get("Contents", []):
                      if files_scanned >= max_files:
                          break
                      key = obj["Key"]
                      size_bytes = obj.get("Size", 0)
                      lower_key = key.lower()

                      if not any(lower_key.endswith(ext) for ext in SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS):
                          files_skipped_unscannable += 1
                          continue
                      if size_bytes == 0:
                          continue

                      finding = _classify_object(access_point_arn, key, size_bytes, language_code)
                      files_scanned += 1

                      if finding["sampled"]:
                          files_sampled_too_large += 1
                      if finding["entity_counts"]:
                          files_with_pii += 1
                          findings.append(finding)
                          for etype, count in finding["entity_counts"].items():
                              pii_density_by_type[etype] = pii_density_by_type.get(etype, 0) + count
                      elif finding["error"]:
                          findings.append(finding)
                  if files_scanned >= max_files:
                      break

              completed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
              report = {
                  "access_point_arn": access_point_arn,
                  "started_at": started_at,
                  "completed_at": completed_at,
                  "language_code": language_code,
                  "files_scanned": files_scanned,
                  "files_skipped_unscannable": files_skipped_unscannable,
                  "files_sampled_too_large": files_sampled_too_large,
                  "files_with_pii": files_with_pii,
                  "pii_density_by_type": pii_density_by_type,
                  "findings": findings[:100],
                  "finding_count": len(findings),
              }

              table = dynamodb.Table(os.environ["REPORT_TABLE_NAME"])
              table.put_item(Item=json.loads(json.dumps(report), parse_float=str))

              logger.info(
                  "Classification complete: %d files scanned, %d with PII, %d unscannable skipped",
                  files_scanned, files_with_pii, files_skipped_unscannable,
              )

              topic_arn = os.environ.get("NOTIFICATION_TOPIC_ARN")
              if topic_arn and files_with_pii > 0:
                  try:
                      sns.publish(
                          TopicArn=topic_arn,
                          Subject=f"[FSx-ONTAP PII Scan] {files_with_pii} file(s) with PII found"[:100],
                          Message=json.dumps(

cfn_description: CloudFormation template for Sera session data ElastiCache Redis infrastructure
cfn_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'CloudFormation template for Sera session data ElastiCache Redis infrastructure'

Parameters:
  StackPrefix:
    Type: String
    Default: sera
    Description: Prefix for all resource names to support multiple SERA deployments
    AllowedPattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{2,20}$'
    ConstraintDescription: Must start with a lowercase letter, contain only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, and be 3-21 characters long

Resources:
  # ElastiCache Subnet Group
  SeraSessionDataSubnetGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElastiCache::SubnetGroup
    Properties:
      CacheSubnetGroupName: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-session-data-subnet-group'
      Description: !Sub 'Subnet group for ${StackPrefix} session data ElastiCache cluster'
      SubnetIds:
        - !ImportValue
          Fn::Sub: '${StackPrefix}-session-db-subnet-1-id'
        - !ImportValue
          Fn::Sub: '${StackPrefix}-session-db-subnet-2-id'
        - !ImportValue
          Fn::Sub: '${StackPrefix}-session-db-subnet-3-id'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Sub 'SERA-${StackPrefix}'
        - Key: StackPrefix
          Value: !Ref StackPrefix

  # Redis AUTH token secret (kept for migration compatibility)
  RedisAuthTokenSecret:
    Type: AWS::SecretsManager::Secret
    Metadata:
      cdk_nag:
        rules_to_suppress:
          - id: AwsSolutions-SMG4
            reason: "This is only to maintain compatibility-uses IAM Auth Tokens for authentication"
    Properties:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-auth-token'
      Description: !Sub 'Redis AUTH token for ${StackPrefix} session data cluster'
      GenerateSecretString:
        PasswordLength: 32
        ExcludeCharacters: '"@/\`~+=[]{}|;:,.*?()_%'
        RequireEachIncludedType: false
        IncludeSpace: false
      KmsKeyId: !ImportValue
          Fn::Sub: '${StackPrefix}-kms-key-arn'
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Sub 'SERA-${StackPrefix}'
        - Key: StackPrefix
          Value: !Ref StackPrefix

  # Custom default User for migration compatibility
  RedisDisabledDefaultUser:
    Type: AWS::ElastiCache::User
    Properties:
      UserId: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-disabled-default'
      UserName: "default"
      AccessString: "off ~* +@all"
      AuthenticationMode:
        Type: "password"
        Passwords:
          - !Sub "{{resolve:secretsmanager:${RedisAuthTokenSecret}:SecretString}}"
      Engine: "redis"
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Sub 'SERA-${StackPrefix}'
        - Key: StackPrefix
          Value: !Ref StackPrefix

  # IAM-based User
  RedisIamUser:
    Type: AWS::ElastiCache::User
    Properties:
      UserId: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-iam-user'
      UserName: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-iam-user'
      AccessString: "on ~* +@all"
      AuthenticationMode:
        Type: "iam"
      Engine: "redis"
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Sub 'SERA-${StackPrefix}'
        - Key: StackPrefix
          Value: !Ref StackPrefix

  # UserGroup containing both users
  RedisUserGroup:
    Type: AWS::ElastiCache::UserGroup
    Properties:
      Engine: "redis"
      UserGroupId: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-user-group'
      UserIds:
        - !Ref RedisDisabledDefaultUser
        - !Ref RedisIamUser
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Sub 'SERA-${StackPrefix}'
        - Key: StackPrefix
          Value: !Ref StackPrefix

  # ElastiCache Replication Group (Redis with replicas)
  SeraSessionDataRedisCluster:
    Type: AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup
    DependsOn: RedisUserGroup
    Properties:
      ReplicationGroupId: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-session-data'
      ReplicationGroupDescription: !Sub 'Redis cluster for ${StackPrefix} session data'
      Engine: redis
      EngineVersion: 7.1
      CacheNodeType: cache.m6g.large
      NumCacheClusters: 2
      MultiAZEnabled: true
      AutomaticFailoverEnabled: true
      TransitEncryptionEnabled: true
      AtRestEncryptionEnabled: true
      KmsKeyId: !ImportValue
          Fn::Sub: '${StackPrefix}-kms-key-id'
      CacheSubnetGroupName: !Ref SeraSessionDataSubnetGroup
      SecurityGroupIds:
        - !ImportValue
          Fn::Sub: '${StackPrefix}-redis-sg-id'
      UserGroupIds:
        - !Sub '${StackPrefix}-user-group'
      Port: 19703
      Tags:
        - Key: Application
          Value: !Sub 'SERA-${StackPrefix}'
        - Key: StackPrefix
          Value: !Ref StackPrefix

Outputs:
  # Redis AUTH token secret
  RedisAuthTokenSecretArn:
    Description: 'ARN of the Redis AUTH token secret'
    Value: !Ref RedisAuthTokenSecret
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-auth-token-secret-arn'

  # ElastiCache outputs
  ElastiCacheEndpoint:
    Description: Primary endpoint for the Redis cluster
    Value: !GetAtt SeraSessionDataRedisCluster.PrimaryEndPoint.Address
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-endpoint'

  ElastiCachePort:
    Description: Port for the Redis cluster
    Value: !GetAtt SeraSessionDataRedisCluster.PrimaryEndPoint.Port
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-port'

  # Hard coded value: Support for CloudFormation error: Template error: resource SeraSessionDataRedisCluster does not support attribute type ReplicationGroupId in Fn::GetAtt even though docs say this is valid
  ReplicationGroupId:
    Description: Replication Group ID
    Value: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-session-data'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-replication-group-id'

  # Replication Group ARN
  ReplicationGroupArn:
    Description: 'ARN of the Redis replication group'
    Value: !Sub 'arn:aws:elasticache:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:replicationgroup:${SeraSessionDataRedisCluster}'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-replication-group-arn'

  # IAM User outputs
  RedisIamUserArn:
    Description: 'ARN of the Redis IAM user'
    Value: !Sub 'arn:aws:elasticache:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:user:${RedisIamUser}'
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-iam-user-arn'

  RedisIamUserName:
    Description: 'Name of the Redis IAM user'
    Value: !Ref RedisIamUser
    Export:
      Name: !Sub '${StackPrefix}-redis-iam-user-name'
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a secure ElastiCache Redis infrastructure for storing session data, using the stack prefix "sera" and importing existing subnet IDs, a KMS key ARN and ID, and a security group ID from the same stack. The template should set up a Redis 7.1 replication group with two cache nodes using cache.m6g.large instances, enable Multi-AZ and automatic failover, enforce transit and at-rest encryption, and use a custom port of 19703. It must also create a subnet group from three imported subnets, a Secrets Manager secret for a Redis AUTH token (generated with a 32-character password excluding special characters) encrypted with the imported KMS key, a disabled default user for migration compatibility using that password, an IAM-based user for modern authentication, and a user group containing both users. The template should export the Redis endpoint, port, replication group ID and ARN, the IAM user ARN and name, and the AUTH token secret ARN for cross-stack references.

#  snippet-service:[appstream2]
#  snippet-keyword:[YAML]
#  snippet-keyword:[Amazon AppStream 2.0]

#  snippet-keyword:[Code Sample]

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: "Sample Amazon Athena queries to analyze Amazon AppStream 2.0 usage reports data"

Resources:
  AverageSessionLengthCurrentMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "Average AppStream 2.0 session length per stack in current month"
      Name: AS2_avg_session_length_curr_mo
      QueryString: "-- Average session length per stack for AppStream 2.0 user sessions launched during the current month
                    -- Each session duration rounded up to whole minute and whole hour before being averaged

                    SELECT stack_name,
                       ROUND(AVG(CEIL(CAST(session_duration_in_seconds AS DOUBLE) / 60)), 2) AS avg_session_length_in_minutes,
                       ROUND(AVG(CEIL(CAST(session_duration_in_seconds AS DOUBLE) / 3600)), 2) AS avg_session_length_in_hours

                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"

                    WHERE
                     year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')

                    GROUP BY stack_name
                    ORDER BY avg_session_length_in_minutes DESC;"

  AverageSessionLengthPreviousMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "Average AppStream 2.0 session length per stack in previous month"
      Name: AS2_avg_session_length_prev_mo
      QueryString: "-- Average session length per stack for AppStream 2.0 user sessions launched during the previous month
                    -- Each session duration rounded up to whole minute and whole hour before being averaged

                    SELECT stack_name,
                       ROUND(AVG(CEIL(CAST(session_duration_in_seconds AS DOUBLE) / 60)), 2) AS avg_session_length_in_minutes,
                       ROUND(AVG(CEIL(CAST(session_duration_in_seconds AS DOUBLE) / 3600)), 2) AS avg_session_length_in_hours

                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"

                    WHERE
                     ((year = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%m'))

                     OR

                     (year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND day <= '05'))

                     AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y-%m-01')
                     AND session_start_time < DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')

                    GROUP BY stack_name
                    ORDER BY avg_session_length_in_minutes DESC;"

  DailySessionsCurrentMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "AppStream 2.0 sessions per day in current month"
      Name: AS2_daily_sessions_curr_mo
      QueryString: "-- Number of AppStream 2.0 sessions per day for the current month

                    SELECT SUBSTRING(session_start_time, 1, 10) AS report_date,
                        COUNT(DISTINCT user_session_id) AS num_sessions
                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"
                    WHERE
                     year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')
                    GROUP BY 1
                    ORDER BY 1"

  DailySessionsPreviousMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "AppStream 2.0 sessions per day in previous month"
      Name: AS2_daily_sessions_prev_mo
      QueryString: "-- Number of AppStream 2.0 sessions per day for the previous month

                    SELECT SUBSTRING(session_start_time, 1, 10) AS report_date,
                        COUNT(DISTINCT user_session_id) AS num_sessions
                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"
                    WHERE
                     ((year = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%m'))

                     OR

                     (year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND day <= '05'))

                     AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y-%m-01')
                     AND session_start_time < DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')
                    GROUP BY 1
                    ORDER BY 1"

  AllAppStreamSessionsCurrentMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "All AppStream 2.0 sessions from current month"
      Name: AS2_sessions_curr_mo
      QueryString: "-- AppStream 2.0 sessions monthly report: all user sessions launched during the current month

                    SELECT *
                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"
                    WHERE
                     year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')
                    ORDER BY session_start_time;"

  AllAppStreamSessionsPreviousMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "All AppStream 2.0 sessions from previous month"
      Name: AS2_sessions_prev_mo
      QueryString: "-- AppStream 2.0 sessions monthly report: all user sessions launched during the previous month

                    SELECT *
                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"
                    WHERE
                     ((year = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%m'))

                     OR

                     (year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND day <= '05'))

                     AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y-%m-01')
                     AND session_start_time < DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')

                    ORDER BY session_start_time;"

  StreamingHoursPerUserCurrentMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "AppStream 2.0 streaming hours per user in current month"
      Name: AS2_users_curr_mo
      QueryString: "-- AppStream 2.0 streaming hours per user in current month
                    -- Each session duration rounded up to whole hour

                    SELECT authentication_type_user_id AS user,
                        SUM(CEIL(CAST(session_duration_in_seconds AS DOUBLE) / 3600)) AS streaming_hours
                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"
                    WHERE
                     year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')
                    GROUP BY 1
                    ORDER BY 2 DESC;"

  StreamingHoursPerUserPreviousMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "AppStream 2.0 streaming hours per user in previous month"
      Name: AS2_users_prev_mo
      QueryString: "-- AppStream 2.0 streaming hours per user in previous month
                      -- Each session duration rounded up to whole hour

                      SELECT authentication_type_user_id AS user,
                          SUM(CEIL(CAST(session_duration_in_seconds AS DOUBLE) / 3600)) AS streaming_hours
                      FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\"
                      WHERE
                       ((year = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y')
                       AND month = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%m'))

                       OR

                       (year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                       AND month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                       AND day <= '05'))

                       AND session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y-%m-01')
                       AND session_start_time < DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')
                     GROUP BY 1
                      ORDER BY 2 DESC;"

  UsersPerApplicationCurrentMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "Users per AppStream 2.0 app in current month"
      Name: AS2_users_per_app_curr_mo
      QueryString: "-- Users per AppStream 2.0 app in current month

                    SELECT DISTINCT apps.application_name, sessions.authentication_type_user_id

                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"applications\" apps
                     INNER JOIN \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\" sessions ON (
                     apps.user_session_id = sessions.user_session_id
                     AND apps.year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND apps.month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m'))

                    WHERE
                     sessions.year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND sessions.month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND sessions.session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')

                    ORDER BY apps.application_name"

  UsersPerApplicationPreviousMonth:
    Type: AWS::Athena::NamedQuery
    Properties:
      Database: appstream-usage
      Description: "Users per AppStream 2.0 app in previous month"
      Name: AS2_users_per_app_prev_mo
      QueryString: "-- Users per AppStream 2.0 app in previous month

                    SELECT DISTINCT apps.application_name, sessions.authentication_type_user_id

                    FROM \"appstream-usage\".\"applications\" apps
                     INNER JOIN \"appstream-usage\".\"sessions\" sessions ON (
                     apps.user_session_id = sessions.user_session_id

                     AND

                     ((apps.year = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y')
                     AND apps.month = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%m'))

                     OR

                     (apps.year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND apps.month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND apps.day <= '05')))

                    WHERE
                     ((sessions.year = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y')
                     AND sessions.month = DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%m'))

                     OR

                     (sessions.year = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y')
                     AND sessions.month = DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%m')
                     AND sessions.day <= '05'))

                     AND sessions.session_start_time >= DATE_FORMAT(date_add('month', -1, current_date), '%Y-%m-01')
                     AND sessions.session_start_time < DATE_FORMAT(current_date, '%Y-%m-01')

                    ORDER BY apps.application_name"
#  snippet-end:[appstream2.yaml.sample-queries-appstream-usage-data-template.complete]
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a set of Amazon Athena named queries for analyzing AppStream 2.0 usage data from an existing database named "appstream-usage", providing pre-built queries for current and previous month comparisons of average session length per stack, daily session counts, all session details, streaming hours per user, and unique users per application, all aimed at simplifying monthly reporting and analysis of AppStream 2.0 session metrics.

cfn_description: Security - Service Control Policies for AWS Organizations - Managed by Platform Team
cfn_code:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"
Description: "Security - Service Control Policies for AWS Organizations - Managed by Platform Team"

# Deploy this in the MANAGEMENT ACCOUNT ONLY via AWS Organizations
# These SCPs are applied to OUs and enforce hard limits that IAM policies cannot override.
#
# CAUTION: Incorrectly written SCPs can lock out all access to an account.
# Test in a sandbox OU before applying to production OUs.

Resources:

  # ============================================================
  # Baseline Security SCP — applied to ALL OUs except Root
  # ============================================================
  BaselineSecuritySCP:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::Policy
    Properties:
      Type: SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY
      Name: "baseline-security-controls"
      Description: "Prevents disabling core security services and enforces security baselines"
      Content: |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Sid": "DenyDisableCloudTrail",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "Action": [
                "cloudtrail:DeleteTrail",
                "cloudtrail:StopLogging",
                "cloudtrail:UpdateTrail"
              ],
              "Resource": "*"
            },
            {
              "Sid": "DenyDisableConfig",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "Action": [
                "config:DeleteConfigRule",
                "config:DeleteConfigurationRecorder",
                "config:DeleteDeliveryChannel",
                "config:StopConfigurationRecorder"
              ],
              "Resource": "*"
            },
            {
              "Sid": "DenyDisableGuardDuty",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "Action": [
                "guardduty:DeleteDetector",
                "guardduty:DisassociateFromMasterAccount",
                "guardduty:DisassociateMembers",
                "guardduty:StopMonitoringMembers",
                "guardduty:UpdateDetector"
              ],
              "Resource": "*"
            },
            {
              "Sid": "DenyDisableSecurityHub",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "Action": [
                "securityhub:DeleteHub",
                "securityhub:DisableSecurityHub",
                "securityhub:DisassociateFromMasterAccount"
              ],
              "Resource": "*"
            },
            {
              "Sid": "DenyLeaveOrganization",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "Action": "organizations:LeaveOrganization",
              "Resource": "*"
            },
            {
              "Sid": "DenyRootActions",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "NotAction": [
                "iam:CreateVirtualMFADevice",
                "iam:EnableMFADevice",
                "iam:GetUser",
                "iam:ListMFADevices",
                "iam:ListVirtualMFADevices",
                "iam:ResyncMFADevice",
                "sts:GetSessionToken"
              ],
              "Resource": "*",
              "Condition": {
                "StringLike": {
                  "aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::*:root"
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        }

  # ============================================================
  # Region Restriction SCP — limit deployments to approved regions
  # ============================================================
  RegionRestrictionSCP:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::Policy
    Properties:
      Type: SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY
      Name: "region-restriction"
      Description: "Restricts deployments to approved AWS regions only"
      Content: |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Sid": "DenyUnapprovedRegions",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "NotAction": [
                "a4b:*",
                "acm:*",
                "aws-marketplace-management:*",
                "aws-marketplace:*",
                "budgets:*",
                "ce:*",
                "chime:*",
                "cloudfront:*",
                "config:*",
                "cur:*",
                "directconnect:*",
                "ec2:DescribeRegions",
                "ec2:DescribeTransitGateways",
                "ec2:DescribeVpnGateways",
                "fms:*",
                "globalaccelerator:*",
                "health:*",
                "iam:*",
                "importexport:*",
                "kms:*",
                "mobileanalytics:*",
                "networkmanager:*",
                "organizations:*",
                "pricing:*",
                "route53:*",
                "route53domains:*",
                "s3:GetAccountPublic*",
                "s3:ListAllMyBuckets",
                "s3:PutAccountPublic*",
                "shield:*",
                "sts:*",
                "support:*",
                "trustedadvisor:*",
                "waf-regional:*",
                "waf:*",
                "wafv2:*",
                "wellarchitected:*"
              ],
              "Resource": "*",
              "Condition": {
                "StringNotIn": {
                  "aws:RequestedRegion": [
                    "eu-west-1",
                    "eu-west-2"
                  ]
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        }

  # ============================================================
  # Production Account SCP — tighter controls for prod OUs
  # ============================================================
  ProductionAccountSCP:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::Policy
    Properties:
      Type: SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY
      Name: "production-account-controls"
      Description: "Additional restrictions for production accounts — no direct console changes"
      Content: |
        {
          "Version": "2012-10-17",
          "Statement": [
            {
              "Sid": "DenyDirectIAMChanges",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "Action": [
                "iam:AttachRolePolicy",
                "iam:CreateRole",
                "iam:DeleteRole",
                "iam:DetachRolePolicy",
                "iam:PutRolePolicy",
                "iam:UpdateRole",
                "iam:CreatePolicy",
                "iam:DeletePolicy",
                "iam:CreatePolicyVersion",
                "iam:DeletePolicyVersion"
              ],
              "Resource": "*",
              "Condition": {
                "ArnNotLike": {
                  "aws:PrincipalArn": [
                    "arn:aws:iam::*:role/GitHubActions-Deploy-prod",
                    "arn:aws:iam::*:role/CloudFormationServiceRole",
                    "arn:aws:iam::*:role/PlatformAdminAccess"
                  ]
                }
              }
            },
            {
              "Sid": "DenyEC2TerminationWithoutTag",
              "Effect": "Deny",
              "Action": "ec2:TerminateInstances",
              "Resource": "*",
              "Condition": {
                "StringNotEquals": {
                  "aws:RequestTag/ManagedBy": "cloudformation"
                }
              }
            }
          ]
        }

Outputs:
  BaselineSCPId:
    Value: !Ref BaselineSecuritySCP
    Description: "Attach this SCP to all OUs except Root and Security OU"

  RegionRestrictionSCPId:
    Value: !Ref RegionRestrictionSCP
    Description: "Attach this SCP to Workloads and Infrastructure OUs"

  ProductionSCPId:
    Value: !Ref ProductionAccountSCP
    Description: "Attach this SCP to the Workloads/Prod OU only"
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates three AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) in the management account: a baseline security SCP preventing disabling of core security services and leaving the organization, a region restriction SCP limiting deployments to only eu-west-1 and eu-west-2, and a production account SCP that denies direct IAM changes except for specific roles (GitHubActions-Deploy-prod, CloudFormationServiceRole, and PlatformAdminAccess) and prevents EC2 termination without a ManagedBy tag set to cloudformation, with the template outputting the SCP IDs for attachment to appropriate OUs.

Parameters:

Resources :

  RestApi :
        Type : AWS::ApiGateway::RestApi
        Properties :
            Body :

                info :
                    version : 0.0.1
                    title : NIH Grants API
                basePath : /

            Name : nihGrantsApi
            Parameters:
                endpointConfigurationTypes: REGIONAL

    DependsOn:  DestQueue
    Type: AWS::ApiGateway::Authorizer
    Properties:
      AuthorizerResultTtlInSeconds: 300
      IdentitySource: method.request.header.Authorization
      Name: CognitoUserPoolAuthorizer
      RestApiId: !Ref RestApi
      Type: COGNITO_USER_POOLS
      ProviderARNs:
         - !Ref COGUPARN

  APIGatewayRole:
      DependsOn:  DestQueue
      Properties:
        AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
          Statement:
            - Action:
                - sts:AssumeRole
              Effect: Allow
              Principal:
                Service:
                  - apigateway.amazonaws.com
          Version: '2012-10-17'
        Path: /
        Policies:
          - PolicyDocument:
              Statement:
                - Action: sqs:SendMessage
                  Effect: Allow
                  Resource: !GetAtt 'DestQueue.Arn'
                - Action:
                    - logs:CreateLogGroup
                    - logs:CreateLogStream
                    - logs:PutLogEvents
                  Effect: Allow
                  Resource: !Sub
                    - >-
                      arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:log-group:${group}
                    - region: !Ref "AWS::Region"
                      account: !Ref "AWS::AccountId"
                      group: !Join ['', ['/aws/apigateway-', !Ref RestApi, '-access-logs']]
                - Effect: Allow
                  Action:
                    - kms:Decrypt
                    - kms:GenerateDataKey
                  Resource: !Sub
                    - >-
                      arn:aws:kms:${region}:${account}:key/${key}
                    - region: !Ref "AWS::Region"
                      account: !Ref "AWS::AccountId"
                      key: !Ref ApiGatewayLogsKMSKey
              Version: '2012-10-17'
            PolicyName: apig-sqs-send-msg-policy
      Type: AWS::IAM::Role

  DestQueue:
      DependsOn:
        - DeadLetterQueue
        - ApiGatewayLogsKMSKey
      Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
      DeletionPolicy: Delete
      UpdateReplacePolicy: Delete
      Properties:
        DelaySeconds: 0
        VisibilityTimeout: 900
        MaximumMessageSize: 262144
        QueueName: !Ref 'queueName'
        ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds: 0
        MessageRetentionPeriod: 60
        RedrivePolicy:
          deadLetterTargetArn: !GetAtt DeadLetterQueue.Arn
          maxReceiveCount: 5

  DeadLetterQueue:
    Type: AWS::SQS::Queue
    DependsOn: ApiGatewayLogsKMSKey

  PolicySQS:
      Type: AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy
      Properties:
        Queues:
          - !Ref 'DestQueue'
        PolicyDocument:
          Version: '2012-10-17'
          Statement:

  ApiGatewayLogsKMSKey:
    Type: 'AWS::KMS::Key'
    Properties:
      Description: 'KMS key for encrypting API Gateway CloudWatch Logs'
      EnableKeyRotation: true
      KeyPolicy:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Sid: 'Enable IAM User Permissions'
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              AWS: !Sub 'arn:aws:iam::${AWS::AccountId}:root'
            Action:
              - 'kms:Create*'
              - 'kms:Describe*'
              - 'kms:Enable*'
              - 'kms:List*'
              - 'kms:Put*'
              - 'kms:Update*'
              - 'kms:Revoke*'
              - 'kms:Disable*'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey'
              - 'kms:Get*'
              - 'kms:Delete*'
              - 'kms:Decrypt'
              - 'kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion'
              - 'kms:CancelKeyDeletion'
            Resource:
              - !Sub 'arn:aws:kms:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:key/*'
          - Sid: 'Allow CloudWatch Logs'
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: !Sub 'logs.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
            Action:
              - 'kms:Encrypt*'
              - 'kms:Decrypt*'
              - 'kms:ReEncrypt*'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey*'
              - 'kms:Describe*'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              ArnLike:
                'kms:EncryptionContext:aws:logs:arn': !Sub 'arn:aws:logs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:*'
          - Sid: 'Allow SQS Service for Specific Queues'
            Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: 'sqs.amazonaws.com'
            Action:
              - 'kms:Encrypt*'
              - 'kms:Decrypt*'
              - 'kms:ReEncrypt*'
              - 'kms:GenerateDataKey*'
              - 'kms:Describe*'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringEquals:
                'kms:ViaService': !Sub 'sqs.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com'
              ArnLike:
                'kms:EncryptionContext:aws:sqs:arn':
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:sqs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${queueName}'
                  - !Sub 'arn:aws:sqs:${AWS::Region}:${AWS::AccountId}:${queueName}-dlq'

  ApiGatewayLogsKMSKeyAlias:
    Type: 'AWS::KMS::Alias'
    Properties:
      AliasName: alias/nih-grants-apigateway-logs-key
      TargetKeyId: !Ref ApiGatewayLogsKMSKey

    Properties:

        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:

            Principal:

AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: 'CloudFormation template for AgentCore Strands Template with Cognito'
Metadata:
  AWS::CloudFormation::Interface:
    ParameterGroups:
      - Label:
          default: Cognito Configuration
        Parameters:
          - UserPoolName
          - MachineAppClientName
          - WebAppClientName

Parameters:

  UserPoolName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'TemplateGatewayPool'
    Description: 'Name of the Cognito User Pool'

  MachineAppClientName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'TemplateMachineClient'
    Description: 'Name of the Cognito User Pool Application Client'

  WebAppClientName:
    Type: String
    Default: 'TemplateWebClient'
    Description: 'Name of the Cognito User Pool Web Application Client'

Resources:

  UserPool:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPool
    Properties:
      UserPoolName: !Ref UserPoolName
      MfaConfiguration: 'OPTIONAL'
      EnabledMfas:
        - SOFTWARE_TOKEN_MFA
      UsernameConfiguration:
        CaseSensitive: false
      UsernameAttributes:
        - email  # <--- Use email as username
      AutoVerifiedAttributes:
        - email  # <--- Auto-verify email if you want to skip confirmation step
      # LambdaConfig:
      #   PostConfirmation: !GetAtt PostSignupFunction.Arn

  AdminGroup:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolGroup
    Properties:
      GroupName: admin
      Description: Administrator group
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Precedence: 1  # Higher priority (lower number = higher precedence)

  CustomerGroup:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolGroup
    Properties:
      GroupName: customer
      Description: Regular customer group
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Precedence: 2

  WebUserPoolClient:
    DependsOn: ResourceServer
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Ref WebAppClientName
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: false  # Don't use secret for SPA or web apps
      AllowedOAuthFlows:
        - code
      AllowedOAuthScopes:
        - openid
        - email
        - profile
        - !Join
            - ''
            - - 'default-m2m-resource-server-'
              - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
              - '/read'
      AllowedOAuthFlowsUserPoolClient: true
      CallbackURLs:
        - http://localhost:8501/
        - https://example.com/auth/callback
      LogoutURLs:
        - http://localhost:8501/
      SupportedIdentityProviders:
        - COGNITO
      AccessTokenValidity: 60
      IdTokenValidity: 60
      RefreshTokenValidity: 30
      TokenValidityUnits:
        AccessToken: minutes
        IdToken: minutes
        RefreshToken: days
      EnableTokenRevocation: true

  MachineUserPoolClient:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolClient
    DependsOn: ResourceServer
    Properties:
      ClientName: !Ref MachineAppClientName
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      GenerateSecret: true
      ExplicitAuthFlows:
        - ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH
      RefreshTokenValidity: 1
      AccessTokenValidity: 60
      IdTokenValidity: 60
      TokenValidityUnits:
        AccessToken: minutes
        IdToken: minutes
        RefreshToken: days
      AllowedOAuthFlows:
        - client_credentials
      AllowedOAuthScopes:
        - !Join
          - ''
          - - 'default-m2m-resource-server-'
            - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
            - '/read'
      AllowedOAuthFlowsUserPoolClient: true
      SupportedIdentityProviders:
        - COGNITO
      EnableTokenRevocation: true

  ResourceServer:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolResourceServer
    Properties:
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Identifier: !Join
        - '-'
        - - 'default-m2m-resource-server'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
      Name: !Join
        - '-'
        - - 'Default M2M Resource Server '
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
      Scopes:
        - ScopeName: 'read'
          ScopeDescription: 'An example scope created by Amazon Cognito quick start'

  UserPoolDomain:
    Type: AWS::Cognito::UserPoolDomain
    Properties:
      UserPoolId: !Ref UserPool
      Domain: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Ref 'AWS::Region'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]

  PostSignupFunctionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service: lambda.amazonaws.com
            Action: sts:AssumeRole
      Policies:
        - PolicyName: AllowBasicLogs
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - logs:CreateLogGroup
                  - logs:CreateLogStream
                  - logs:PutLogEvents
                Resource: arn:aws:logs:*:*:*
        - PolicyName: Cognito
          PolicyDocument:
            Version: '2012-10-17'
            Statement:
              - Effect: Allow
                Action:
                  - cognito-idp:AdminAddUserToGroup
                Resource: "*"

  PostSignupFunction:
    Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
    Properties:
      Handler: index.lambda_handler
      Runtime: python3.13
      Role: !GetAtt PostSignupFunctionRole.Arn
      Timeout: 10
      Code:
        ZipFile: |
          import boto3

          def lambda_handler(event, context):
              user_pool_id = event['userPoolId']
              username = event['userName']
              client = boto3.client('cognito-idp')

              # Add user to 'customer' group
              try:
                  client.admin_add_user_to_group(
                      UserPoolId=user_pool_id,
                      Username=username,
                      GroupName='Customer'
                  )
                  print(f"User {username} added to 'customer' group.")
              except Exception as e:
                  print(f"Error adding user to group: {e}")

              return event

  CognitoMachineClientIdParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/machine_client_id
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref MachineUserPoolClient
      Description: Machine Cognito client ID
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoMachineClientSecretParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_secret
      Type: String
      Value: !GetAtt MachineUserPoolClient.ClientSecret
      Description: Machine Cognito client secret
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoWebClientIdParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/web_client_id
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref WebUserPoolClient
      Description: Cognito client ID for web app
      Tags:
        Application: CustomerSuppor

  UserPoolIdParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/userpool_id
      Type: String
      Value: !Ref UserPool
      Description: Cognito client ID
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoAuthScopeParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_auth_scope
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - 'default-m2m-resource-server-'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - '/read'
      Description: OAuth2 scope for Cognito auth
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoDiscoveryURLParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_discovery_url
      Type: String
      Value: !Sub 'https://cognito-idp.${AWS::Region}.amazonaws.com/${UserPool}/.well-known/openid-configuration'
      Description: OAuth2 Discovery URL
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoTokenURLParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_token_url
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - !Sub '.auth.${AWS::Region}.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/token'
      Description: OAuth2 Token URL
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoAuthorizeURLParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_auth_url
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - !Sub '.auth.${AWS::Region}.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/authorize'
      Description: OAuth2 Token URL
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp

  CognitoDomainParameter:
    Type: AWS::SSM::Parameter
    Properties:
      Name: /app/researchapp/agentcore/cognito_domain
      Type: String
      Value: !Join
        - ''
        - - !Sub 'https://${AWS::Region}'
          - !Select [0, !Split ['-', !Select [2, !Split ['/', !Ref 'AWS::StackId']]]]
          - !Sub '.auth.${AWS::Region}.amazoncognito.com'
      Description: Cognito hosted domain for OAuth2
      Tags:
        Application: researchapp
user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a Cognito user pool for an application called "researchapp" and "AgentCore", with MFA set to optional using software tokens, email as username and auto-verified, and two user groups (admin and customer) where the customer group has higher precedence. The template should include a web app client using the authorization code flow with callback URLs set to http://localhost:8501/ and https://example.com/auth/callback, and a machine-to-machine client using client credentials flow with a generated secret. Both clients should use a custom resource server with a read scope. Additionally, a Lambda function triggered by post-confirmation should automatically add new users to the customer group. All relevant configuration—such as client IDs, secrets, user pool ID, OAuth scopes, discovery URL, token URL, authorize URL, and the Cognito domain—must be stored in SSM Parameter Store under the path /app/researchapp/agentcore/. The template should accept three parameters with defaults: UserPoolName (TemplateGatewayPool), MachineAppClientName (TemplateMachineClient), and WebAppClientName (TemplateWebClient).

user_prompt: We need a CloudFormation template that creates a scheduled workflow to automatically close AWS Organization accounts that are tagged with the key "organizations:account-closure" and value "REQUESTED". The workflow should run every hour via an EventBridge rule, invoking an EXPRESS Step Functions state machine that paginates through accounts tagged for closure, describes each account, and if it is ACTIVE, closes it using the Organizations CloseAccount API, then tags the account with "ACKNOWLEDGED". The state machine must include error handling for throttling and eventual consistency, log all execution data to a CloudWatch log group with a 365-day retention, and use IAM roles with least-privilege permissions scoped to the required Organizations and tagging actions.
